topics.name: Comparisons with as ... as / not so ... as

options: Meera is as busier as a bee today.
Meera is so busy as a bee today.
Meera is as busy as a bee today.
questions.rule: In as ... as use the plain adjective: as busy as. 'So ... as' is used only after not.
Passive = be + past participle. Honey is uncountable, so: is made.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Between as ... as we use the plain form: as fast as.
as + plain adjective + as: as slow as a snail.
For animals and things the subject relative pronoun is which (or that).

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the passive voice.
questions.rule: Passive: object first, then was + past participle, then by + the doer.

chat: How was your new cousin at the party?
options: He was as quietly as a mouse all evening.
He was as quiet as a mouse all evening.
He were as quiet as a mouse all evening.
questions.rule: After was we need an adjective: as quiet as. With he use was.

chat: Who painted this lovely poster of bees?
options: It was paint by Sana and me.
It were painted by Sana and me.
It was painted by Sana and me.
questions.rule: Past passive with a singular subject: it was painted.
Simple present active becomes is/are + past participle: nectar is collected.

questions.source: A giraffe is taller than a horse.
options: A horse is not as tall as a giraffe.
A horse is as tall as a giraffe.
A horse is not as taller as a giraffe.
questions.rule: Swap the two and use not as + plain adjective + as: a horse is not as tall as a giraffe.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct relative pronoun.
options: The boy which keeps bees lives next door.
The boy who keeps bees lives next door.
The boy whose keeps bees lives next door.
questions.rule: For a person use who as the subject of the clause.

options: The porter bees carried their heavy burdens carefully.
The porter bees carried their heavy burdens careful.
The porter bees carried their heavily burdens carefully.
questions.rule: An adjective describes a noun (heavy burdens); an adverb describes a verb (carried carefully).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Hundreds of bees is plural, so the verb is buzz, not buzzes.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive needs the past participle: was collected.
The roof does not make anything; it is made. Passive: is made.
To describe how he yawned (a verb), use the adverb lazily.
The clause who sells honey comes right after the noun it describes: a beekeeper.

options: Open the one which has a yellow lid.
Open the one who has a yellow lid.
Open the one whose has a yellow lid.
questions.rule: A jar is a thing, so use which.

questions.source: I know a farmer. He keeps fifty beehives.
options: I know a farmer who he keeps fifty beehives.
I know a farmer which keeps fifty beehives.
I know a farmer who keeps fifty beehives.
questions.rule: who replaces he, so do not repeat the pronoun: a farmer who keeps ...

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: There are + plural (three beehives). Passive: honey is sold.

options: The elephant is not as bigger as the blue whale.
The elephant is not as big than the blue whale.
The elephant is not as big as the blue whale.
questions.rule: The pattern is not as + plain adjective + as, never 'than' and never -er.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The girl did the winning, so the relative pronoun is the subject: who, not whom.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: merrily (adverb) tells us how they marched.

questions.after: bees won a prize at the fair.
questions.rule: whose shows possession: the bees belong to the girl.
After not we can use so ... as: not so strict as.

chat: Is the new bus as fast as the old one?
options: No, it is not as fast as the old one.
No, it is not as faster as the old one.
No, it does not as fast as the old one.
questions.rule: Answer an is question with is not as fast as; keep the plain adjective.

chat: Has either of your friends tasted this honey?
options: Yes, each of them have tasted it.
Yes, each of them has tasted it.
Yes, each of them tasting it.
questions.rule: Each of them is singular, so use has.

questions.source: The bees were building a new comb.
options: A new comb was built by the bees.
A new comb were being built by the bees.
A new comb was being built by the bees.
questions.rule: Past continuous passive: was/were being + past participle. One comb, so was being built.

questions.source: The bees live in a hive. It hangs from the neem tree.
options: The bees live in a hive which hangs from the neem tree.
The bees live in a hive which it hangs from the neem tree.
The bees live in a hive which hang from the neem tree.
questions.rule: which replaces it and refers to one hive, so the verb is hangs.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: as sweet as uses the plain adjective; packed carefully needs an adverb.

options: The new hive has been placed near the window.
The new hive has been place near the window.
The new hive have been placed near the window.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle. One hive: has been placed.

options: The beekeeper which visited us yesterday has gone home.
The beekeeper who visits us yesterday has gone home.
The beekeeper who visited us yesterday has gone home.
questions.rule: A person takes who, and yesterday needs the past: visited.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: calmly (adverb) tells us how the bees had settled; an adjective cannot describe a verb.
Modal passive: must be + past participle.
The second as needs a first one: not as hot as.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence in the passive voice.
questions.rule: Future passive: will be + past participle: will be sold.

chat: Have the project files been submitted?
options: Yes, all of them have been submitted.
Yes, all of them have been submit.
Yes, all of them has been submitted.
questions.rule: All of them is plural: have been submitted (past participle).

questions.source: The farmer has sold all the honey.
options: All the honey was sold by the farmer.
All the honey has been sold by the farmer.
All the honey has been sell by the farmer.
questions.rule: Keep the tense: present perfect active has sold becomes has been sold.

questions.source: No other insect is as busy as the bee.
options: The bee is busiest than any other insect.
The bee is more busier than any other insect.
The bee is busier than any other insect.
questions.rule: 'No other ... as busy as' becomes busier than any other. Never 'more busier'.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: which refers to beehives (plural): hang. Passive: be sold. Subject for a person: who.

options: Neither the queen bee nor the workers are resting.
Neither the queen bee nor the workers is resting.
Neither the queen bee or the workers are resting.
questions.rule: With neither ... nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject: the workers are.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Every + singular noun takes a singular verb: every worker bee carries.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The book belongs to the scientist, so use the possessive whose.

questions.before: Not one of the hundreds of bees in the hive
questions.rule: The subject is not one (singular), so use is, even though 'bees' comes just before.
Modal perfect passive: should have been + past participle.

chat: Is your new phone better than your old one?
options: No, it isn't nearly as better as my old one.
No, it isn't nearly so good than my old one.
No, it isn't nearly as good as my old one.
questions.rule: not nearly as good as: plain adjective between as ... as.

chat: What happened to the old beehive behind the shed?
options: It has taken away by the forest officers.
It has been took away by the forest officers.
It has been taken away by the forest officers.
questions.rule: The hive did not take anything; it has been taken (has been + past participle).

options: By whom were the bees disturbed?
By whom was the bees disturbed?
questions.rule: Who becomes By whom; the bees are plural, so were ... disturbed.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: A farm which belongs; passive is extracted; a past visit, so the honey tasted as sweet as jaggery.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Subject for a person: who; passive: be produced; every farmer (singular) knows.
